Hi Julia —

Appreciate the clarity on volumes. I attached a short pricing matrix (Redwood_Pricing_1M_tokens.xlsx) — highlights below so you can share with procurement quickly:

Pricing summary (examples, list price):
- Standard Tier: $120 / 1M tokens — best for batched workloads, expected p95 ~400–600ms depending on model size and prompt length.
- Premium Tier (SLO-backed): $260 / 1M tokens — includes priority capacity, autoscale buffer, and an SLA target for p95 ~200–300ms and p99~350ms (region dependent).
- Enterprise Dedicated (reserved capacity): custom pricing — predictable throughput for high-volume customers (we can run TCO for your projected 4M tokens/mo).

Notes on streaming vs batching:
- Streaming (small batches / single-token flush) gives the lowest latency per token but increases GPU utilization and per-token compute cost — typically 20–40% higher cost vs heavy batching, depending on request shape.
- Batching (accumulate requests to improve GPU throughput) reduces $/token but increases tail latency. Good for asynchronous or non-real-time slices.
- Hybrid: route critical alerts to a Premium streaming pool and chat traffic to a batched pool; smart routing keeps costs down while meeting p99 SLO for the hot path.

Attached MAP includes milestones and procurement items (PO template + required compliance docs). If procurement needs a formal quote, we can push a DocuSign link once you confirm the tier.

Next steps:
- Can Neha run a brief note on recommended batch sizes / expected percent cost delta for your expected payloads?
- Schedule technical deep-dive: Tue 2026-05-26 10:00 PT (proposed). I’ll send a calendar invite.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with the MAP + DocuSign link after the call.

Best,
Marissa

Subject: RE: technical notes — batching, streaming, and unit economics

Hi Julia — quick technical note on the trade-offs and suggested config for your two flows (chat vs alerts).

Summary (short):
- Alerts (p99 < 200ms): use a streaming-first pool with very small batching (1–4 tokens) and reserved priority capacity. Expect ~30–45% increase in $/token vs a heavily batched baseline because of lower GPU efficiency. Optimizations: smaller model head, quantization, and aggressive KV prefix caching for repeated context can reduce that delta to ~15–25%.
- Chat (p95 ~300ms): run on a batched pool (batch size 8–16) with dynamic batching windows (10–30ms). This typically yields the best $/token (our Standard Tier numbers).

Unit economics example (rough estimates for planning):
- Baseline (batched chat, 1M tokens): compute + infra ~ $100 / 1M tokens (model/compute only) — aligns with Standard Tier list price $120 after infra & overhead.
- Streaming alerts (1M tokens equivalent volume, but mostly single-token streaming): compute + infra ~ $140–$160 / 1M tokens before optimizations — maps to Premium Tier pricing when you include priority and SLA overhead.

Routing recommendation: keep a small Premium streaming pool for the alerts (reserve capacity for your busiest 5–10% of traffic) and route the rest to the batched pool. We can automate routing rules by tag or route id so your app decides per-request.

Operational notes:
- We’ll surface a per-route latency/cost dashboard in Redwood Console so you can see dollars per route and token breakdowns.
- For procurement: if you commit to 3–4M tokens/mo we can model a blended committed rate that gets you closer to your $200 / 1M target — I’ll include a sample committed pricing row in the MAP.

Happy to run a short perf test with sample payloads during the pilot week to produce concrete numbers.

— Neha
